title: Target-Span Conditions for Transporting Intervention Laws with Proxies under Latent Shift
banked_reason: Re-tiered from accepted on 2026-09-09: fully proved in Lean and originally accepted at field tier, but re-scored 6.9 under the recalibrated D0.5.G scale, below the 7.2 field bar; the mathematics was not refuted.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the target-span identification equivalence, solution independence, a strictly positive full-law converse, finite-sample projection coverage, and the impossibility of uniformly studentized Wald adaptation. The final proof used the promoted rank-one spectral-projector and pseudoinverse smoothness substrate; all graph obligations were delivered with no added assumptions, gates, or sorry axioms.
tldr: A target intervention law can remain identified even when source environments do not span the latent state space. In the strictly positive finite latent-shift SCM, injectivity of the unknown proxy channel turns the observable condition \(b=Q(W)\in\operatorname{col}(B_x)\), with \(B_x=P_O(W\mid E,x)\), into the exact identification frontier. Every solution of \(B_x\lambda=b\) gives the same functional \(c_{x,y}\lambda\). Off the span, an observed separator lifts to a proxy-stratum outcome perturbation that preserves the full source and target proxy laws while moving the causal effect through an interval. A concentration-calibrated Anderson--Rubin-style projection set has finite-sample coverage without rank or weight bounds. The note additionally records a limitation of its deliberately unrestricted changing-rank array class: uniform coverage cannot also be required to localize to a regular Wald interval without further restrictions.
gap: Iglesias-Alonso et al. require full source rank and lose identification in their counterexample by making the proxy channel noninjective. Zhang et al. settle constancy of abstract bridge functionals, and Rahiminasab et al. use full source rank over proxy-equivalence classes for prediction. None gives the target-specific causal if-and-only-if result over the full observed-law SCM fiber with an injective proxy channel.
fill: The project proves sufficiency, solution independence, and an input-specific positive full-law converse; supplies an exact rational rank-deficient success witness; and attaches finite-sample projection coverage plus a sharply stated studentized weak-rank inference question.
